knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $4 x^{2} + 4 x - 4 y=-8$. The **normal** line at $\left(-2,4\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
8 x + 4+\left(-4\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(-4\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(8 x + 4\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{8 x + 4}{-4}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-12}{-4}=-3
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{-3}=\frac{1}{3}
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(4\right)&=\frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(-2\right)\right) \\
y&=\frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(-2\right)\right)+\left(4\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(-2\right)\right)+\left(4\right) \\
x-\left(-2\right)&=-\frac{4}{\frac{1}{3}} \\
x&=-14
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(-14,0\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $4 x^{2} - 2 x + 4 y^{2} + 4 y=30$. The **normal** line at $\left(-1,-3\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
8 x - 2+\left(8 y + 4\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(8 y + 4\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(8 x - 2\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{8 x - 2}{8 y + 4}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-10}{-20}=- \frac{1}{2}
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{- \frac{1}{2}}=2
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-3\right)&=2\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right) \\
y&=2\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)+\left(-3\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=2\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)+\left(-3\right) \\
x-\left(-1\right)&=-\frac{-3}{2} \\
x&=\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(\frac{1}{2},0\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $- 2 x y - y^{2}=0$. The **normal** line at $\left(-2,4\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. The product rule gives $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=y+x\frac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
- 2 y+\left(- 2 x - 2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(- 2 x - 2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(- 2 y\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{- 2 y}{- 2 x - 2 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-8}{-4}=-2
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{-2}=\frac{1}{2}
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(4\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-2\right)\right) \\
y&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-2\right)\right)+\left(4\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=\frac{1}{2}\left(0-\left(-2\right)\right)+\left(4\right) \\
y&=5
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,5\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x^{2} + 3 y^{2}=4$. The **normal** line at $\left(1,1\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 x+\left(6 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(6 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(2 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{2 x}{6 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{2}{6}=- \frac{1}{3}
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{- \frac{1}{3}}=3
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=3\left(x-\left(1\right)\right) \\
y&=3\left(x-\left(1\right)\right)+\left(1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=3\left(x-\left(1\right)\right)+\left(1\right) \\
x-\left(1\right)&=-\frac{1}{3} \\
x&=\frac{2}{3}
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(\frac{2}{3},0\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x y + 2 x - y=5$. The **normal** line at $\left(4,-1\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. The product rule gives $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=y+x\frac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y + 2+\left(x - 1\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(x - 1\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(y + 2\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{y + 2}{x - 1}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{1}{3}=- \frac{1}{3}
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{- \frac{1}{3}}=3
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-1\right)&=3\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\
y&=3\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(-1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=3\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(-1\right) \\
x-\left(4\right)&=-\frac{-1}{3} \\
x&=\frac{13}{3}
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(\frac{13}{3},0\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x^{2} - 4 x - 2 y=-2$. The **normal** line at $\left(4,1\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 x - 4+\left(-2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(-2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(2 x - 4\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{2 x - 4}{-2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{4}{-2}=2
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{2}=- \frac{1}{2}
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=- \frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\
y&=- \frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{1}{2}\left(0-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(1\right) \\
y&=3
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,3\right)$.
